prompt: How does the graph of $y = \sin\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ compare with the graph of $y = \sin(x)$?
hint: A change inside the parentheses moves the graph sideways, not up and down.

hints.text: A change inside the parentheses moves the graph sideways, not up and down.
Ask where the curve now starts its cycle: you need $x - \frac{\pi}{3} = 0$.
$x = \frac{\pi}{3}$, so the cycle begins $\frac{\pi}{3}$ later — a shift to the right.

explanation: Subtracting inside the function moves the graph horizontally.
The cycle used to start where the input was $0$, which was $x = 0$; now the input is $0$ when $x = \frac{\pi}{3}$.
So every feature of the wave happens $\frac{\pi}{3}$ later: the graph slides right by $\frac{\pi}{3}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The minus sign feels backwards on purpose
steps: A minus inside always shifts right, and a plus inside always shifts left.
Think of it as the graph running late: it has to wait until $x$ reaches $\frac{\pi}{3}$ before it can do what it used to do at $0$.
